geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant mass from a simple translated block into a continuous bent gesture that can better respond to the parcel and create a clearer urban edge.
Use a plan bend so the form remains one mass while better addressing the access edge and parcel orientation.
Introduce a modest bend rather than a severe split; the goal is continuity, not fragmentation.
Replace the clipped notch with a real courtyard void so the open-space figure becomes legible and programmatic.
Make the courtyard large enough to function as public space, not a minor trim.
Align the void with the verified access side so the street edge reads as an entry threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Retarget the dominant bar into a more legible continuous spatial gesture instead of a mostly straight translated block; this can help align the mass with the parcel and access edge.
Shift the dominant mass slightly to preserve a cleaner anchor and better articulate the public threshold toward the access side.
Convert the notch-like subtraction into a clearer public void so the ground condition reads as usable neighborhood space rather than a clipped corner.
Enlarge the void enough to become legible from multiple views and support a public court/terrace relationship.
Open the public void toward the verified access side so the edge becomes semantically active rather than sealed.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent elongated mass in plan and at least loosely responds to the parcel and access edge, but the visible section is not yet convincing for neighborhood living. The dominant body is understandable, yet the front/ground response is weak: the blue access edge is met by a mostly sealed or semantically ambiguous edge rather than a clearly public court, seam, or undercut. Across views there is also a strong stepped/notched articulation that risks reading as arbitrary tiering rather than a capacity-bearing inhabited section. Because the mass is coherent in some views but the void logic and access relationship are underdeveloped, it fails hard pass on program fit and access response.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More single-story pavilion than this candidate; useful for access/threshold logic but not for the candidate’s stepped multi-part section.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact low-rise street building with a clear public threshold and a simple attached volume language.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much more vertical and urban-block based; do not copy the tall slab proportion.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Attached streetwall pieces with a setback and offset massing can support neighborhood mixed-use without fragmenting the whole.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual: this image demonstrates a much larger, more continuous inhabited-section landform; transferring the principle requires keeping the active ground edge and avoiding oversized swooping roofscape.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/courtyard massing can work when the void is sectionally meaningful and tied to upper circulation.

warnings: Parcel containment appears respected, but the open-space figure is underpowered relative to the site access edge.
The form is more legible as a carved bar than as an active neighborhood threshold.
Stepped extrusion language is present, but the section does not yet earn the step as programmatic rather than decorative.
